DPI Closes $112M Nclude Fund Backed Mostly by Local Capital

이 제목은 아래 게시물에서 AI가 요약한 것입니다.

𝐃𝐏𝐈 𝐂𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐞𝐬 $𝟏𝟏𝟐 𝐌𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐀𝐟𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐜𝐡 𝐅𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐁𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐞𝐝 𝐌𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐥𝐲 𝐛𝐲 𝐋𝐨𝐜𝐚𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 DPI Venture Capital has reached a final close of more than $112 million for its Nclude Fund, with 93% of committed capital originating from African investors, according to managing partner Ashley Lewis. Financial services institutions account for nearly all the fund's investor base, providing a source of institutional financing for fintech companies across Africa and the Middle East. Nclude currently holds investments in 15 businesses and can invest between $500,000 and $10 million per company, from seed funding through Series C. Established in Egypt in 2022 with backing from financial institutions including Banque Misr, the fund came under DPI's advisory management in 2025. Its portfolio includes payments provider Paymob, digital savings platform Money Fellows and property technology company Nawy. DPI has broadened the fund's geographical mandate, allowing up to 30% of capital to be deployed beyond Egypt, and expects the portfolio to expand to between 22 and 24 companies. The final close provides an example of African financial institutions committing capital to venture investing, although the fund's total is below its original $150 million fundraising ambition.
